reason: Weighty bills change who appoints Supreme Court judges and its president and the selection committee's makeup; the statement asks exactly that.

statements.new_statement_en: The Jewish character of the state and its Jewish majority should be anchored more firmly in law, even if non-Jews feel less equal.

reason: Heaviest bills are immigration Basic Laws (Jewish majority) plus nation-state and Declaration laws; oath bills are minor, so drop the oath example and name the Jewish majority.
Basic Law: Torah Study and the draft/equal-burden bills carry nearly all weight and directly concern drafting yeshiva students.
Most weight is illegal-stay, entry, citizenship/family-unification and Law of Return relatives bills, matching the statement; hostile-institutions and Area C bills are off.
UNRWA ban, foreign missions in Jerusalem, hostile international institutions and foreign-state funding bills all restrict foreign and international activity in Israel.

split.plus_en: Fewer legal conditions and approvals for ending a pregnancy
split.minus_en: More legal conditions and approvals for ending a pregnancy
split.statement_en: A woman should have the right to an abortion without approval from a hospital pregnancy-termination committee, even if there are more abortions.

split.plus_en: Wider legal access to and funding of surrogacy, egg donation, fertility preservation and posthumous sperm use
split.minus_en: Narrower access to these fertility technologies
split.statement_en: The law should widen access to surrogacy, egg donation and other fertility technologies, even if this contradicts Jewish religious law.

reason: Abortion and assisted reproduction are distinct issues; posthumous sperm and fertility preservation bills carry much weight and fit neither current statement, so split into two.
Bills limit rabbinical court delays, sanction get refusers, allow civil divorce and prenups: all make divorce easier even when a spouse objects.
Most bills raise pay, benefits or job security of firefighters, teachers, police and outsourced workers; forensic-authority, weekly-rest and car-use bills are off-topic.
Except the KKL nationalisation bill (about 36% of weight, off-topic, should be dropped), the bills privatise Kan and Galei Tzahal, matching the statement.

split.name_en: State power to block broadcasts and online content
split.plus_en: Less state power to shut down broadcasters, censor or remove content
split.minus_en: More state power to shut down broadcasters, censor or remove content
split.statement_en: The state should be able to shut down broadcasters and remove online content it considers harmful, even if the public receives less information.

split.name_en: Broadcasting and transparency of court and public-body proceedings
split.plus_en: More filming, broadcasting and publication of court hearings and public meetings
split.minus_en: Less filming, broadcasting and publication of such proceedings
split.statement_en: Court hearings and meetings of public bodies should be filmed and broadcast, even if this affects how participants behave.

reason: Weighty bills are mostly censorship (Al Jazeera law, content removal, denial ban) unrelated to sports; court-transparency bills form a second issue. Sports has one light bill.

split.name_en: State support for settlements in Judea and Samaria
split.plus_en: More state support, benefits, regularisation and expansion of settlements
split.statement_en: The state should reduce its support for settlements in Judea and Samaria (the West Bank), even if this makes life there harder for settlers.

split.plus_en: Applying Israeli law and sovereignty to all or parts of the West Bank
split.minus_en: Not applying sovereignty; recognising a Palestinian state
split.statement_en: Israel should apply its sovereignty to Judea and Samaria (the West Bank), or to parts of it, even at the cost of conflict with allies.

All main-role bills amend the defamation law (war-crimes accusations, public figures, anonymous posters); heavy off bills are spillover from publication-ban and content-removal laws.
Weighty bills open food, banking, finance, transport and broadcasting markets to competitors or favour local suppliers in procurement; this is the statement's trade-off.

statements.new_statement_en: The opposition should have more power in the Knesset and local councils, such as chairing key committees, even if the coalition finds it harder to govern.

reason: Bills cover committee chairs, recess convening, local-council opposition and council members' powers; committee chairs alone is too narrow.

split.name_en: Procedural rights of suspects and defendants
split.plus_en: Stronger protections in arrest, search, questioning, evidence and trial
split.minus_en: More police and prosecution powers, weaker protections
split.statement_en: Suspects and defendants should have fewer legal protections during arrest, questioning and trial, even if more innocent people are wrongly accused.

split.plus_en: No death penalty or citizenship revocation for terrorists
split.minus_en: Death penalty, citizenship revocation and harsher sentences for terrorists
split.statement_en: Convicted terrorists should face harsher penalties, such as death or loss of citizenship, even if this draws international criticism.

reason: Most weight is death penalty and citizenship revocation for terrorists, a punishment issue distinct from procedural rights; questioning without a lawyer covers only a sliver.
Bills protect apartment buyers, workers, athletes and consumers, cap lawyer fees or deregulate notary fees: state intervention in contract terms, as asked.

statements.new_statement_en: Personal information should be better protected by law, even if this makes it harder for the police and the media to obtain it.

reason: Victims' names bills are a small part; weighty bills cover evidence exclusion, data erasure, privileges, publishing prisoners' identities and police data access: privacy generally.

statements.new_statement_en: State funding for religious schools should depend on meeting state conditions, such as teaching core subjects, even if the schools lose independence.

reason: Bills condition funding on core curriculum, non-discriminatory admission and not encouraging draft evasion; admission discrimination alone is too narrow.
The dominant AG law and AG-splitting bills make legal advice less binding on ministers, exactly what the statement asks.
Incapacity law, immunity and indicted-PM bills fit; the many off bills (memorial, drug authority, press conferences) are an incoherent remainder and should be dropped.

statements.new_statement_en: Israel should honour international conventions, its commitments to the UN and the agreements it has signed, even when they limit the government's freedom of action.

reason: About 85% of weight is the UNRWA ban and UN immunities, i.e. obligations to the UN; Oslo is minor, so name UN commitments instead.
